Finding / technology: Android Health Connect: on-device store and API for heart rate, steps, sleep and exercise from many wearables and apps
Impact on the project: High. One integration covers Fitbit, Samsung, Garmin (via sync) and others. On-device = easier GDPR

Finding / technology: Apple HealthKit: iOS equivalent with per-type user permissions
Impact on the project: High if we support iOS. Per-type permission fits modular, opt-in data

Finding / technology: Google Health API replaces the legacy Fitbit Web API (legacy support ends 30 Sep 2026); restricted scopes need a security review
Reference: Google Health API docs; Fitbit community (2026)
Impact on the project: Medium. Only for server-side wearable data. Prefer T1 for the prototype

Finding / technology: Phone context APIs: activity recognition, geofencing, screen and app-use state
Impact on the project: High. Gives a "phone-only" data tier (Quit Sense-style location triggers) without a wearable

Finding / technology: Cross-platform frameworks (Flutter / React Native) with health plugins (e.g. Flutter health package for Health Connect + HealthKit)
Impact on the project: Medium–High. One codebase for both platforms; the agentic-coding-friendly route

Finding / technology: Open mHealth schemas: open JSON schemas for mobile health data (heart rate, step count, survey answers)
Impact on the project: Medium. Use as an internal data model so data tiers stay swappable

Finding / technology: RADAR-base: Apache-2.0 platform for passive sensing, wearables and questionnaires (Kafka-based)
Impact on the project: Low–Medium. Too heavy for our app; good reference for the data pipeline and consent design

Finding / technology: mindLAMP: open-source (BSD-3) digital-phenotyping + survey + intervention platform
Reference: Vaidyam et al. (2022), JMIR mHealth (verify authors)
Impact on the project: Low–Medium. Option for a quick sensing pilot; not our end-user app

Finding / technology: m-Path: EMA / ecological momentary intervention platform from KU Leuven (proprietary, free tiers for research; verify)
Impact on the project: Medium. Fastest way to run a short EMA diary study with smokers before our own app is ready

Finding / technology: BCIO + BCTO as OWL (GitHub, BioPortal), CC BY 4.0
Impact on the project: High. The intervention catalogue schema: each building block = BCTO IDs + mode of delivery + setting

Finding / technology: Theory & Techniques Tool (TaTT): BCT ↔ mechanism-of-action links with evidence strength
Impact on the project: High. Priors for the selector and source text for "why" explanations

Finding / technology: Python ontology/graph tooling (owlready2, rdflib) for querying OWL at runtime
Impact on the project: Medium. Enough to keep the knowledge layer live, with no triple store needed

Finding / technology: HBCP interpretable outcome predictor for smoking-cessation interventions
Reference: Hastings et al. (2023/2025); West et al. (2023/2024)
Impact on the project: Medium. Population-level prior on which BCT combinations work for which population

Finding / technology: Thompson-sampling bandit designs with pooling and safety constraints, published with algorithm details (HeartSteps, Oralytics, MiWaves)
Reference: Liao et al. (2020); Trella et al. (2024); Ghosh et al. (2024); Tomkins et al. (2021)
Impact on the project: High. Blueprint for the fast learner (building-block choice); copy the design, write our own small implementation

Finding / technology: Bandit libraries: Vowpal Wabbit (contextual bandits), MABWiser
Impact on the project: Low–Medium. Baselines in simulation. Our own Bayesian model stays more explainable

Finding / technology: StepCountJITAI: Gymnasium RL simulator with habituation, disengagement and between-person variability
Impact on the project: High. Start for our simulator; replace physical-activity dynamics with smoking dynamics

Finding / technology: COMPLAPSE: computational lapse-risk model for smokers (R, GitHub), proposed for use in RL controllers
Impact on the project: High. Smoking dynamics for T16. Possible collaboration

Finding / technology: UCL EMA + Fitbit lapse dataset (n = 38, 6,124 EMAs), participants consented to open sharing (repository to confirm)
Impact on the project: Medium. Calibrate the simulator and test the "what does each data tier add?" ablation

Finding / technology: Structured conversational frameworks: Rasa Pro (CALM: LLM understanding + deterministic flows; free ≤ 1,000 conversations/month); Rasa Open Source in maintenance mode
Impact on the project: Medium–High. Fits a schema-constrained intake and phase-review chatbot. Alternative: own state machine + LLM calls

Finding / technology: LLM APIs and open-weight models for NLU, MI reflections and message variation
Reference: Brown et al. (2023); Haag et al. (2025)
Impact on the project: High as a component, never the decision maker. Choose EU processing; log model version

Finding / technology: LLM safety: physician red-teaming found many unsafe answers to patient questions across four major chatbots; crisis handling is inconsistent across models
Impact on the project: High. Requires guard-rails: constrained generation, a checker, crisis escalation to human help (Tabakstop, 1813)
